signal: Sirona Medical secured a $45M Series C and is scaling adoption of its cloud-native Unify radiology platform

email.body1:
Blair, saw Sirona Medical close its $45M Series C and lean into scaling adoption of the Unify platform.

Scaling adoption that fast usually widens the signal-to-action gap: in-market accounts surface faster than reps can research, write, and follow up. Our AI SDR handles that autonomously, so coverage scales without new headcount, 3-5x more meetings per rep.

I built a personalized signal play for Sirona off your hiring and tech-stack signals, and accounts showing them progress about 4.4x faster. Worth 15 minutes for me to walk you through it?
email.body2:
Blair, quick follow-up for Sirona.

For RevOps, the hard part is rarely the signal, it is the latency from signal to a booked meeting, plus the data hygiene that keeps it measurable. Most teams lose lift in that handoff, especially post-raise.

Want to grab 15 minutes? I will walk you through a teardown of your current outbound and three things I would change. Our best practices alone usually lift response rates 50 to 70 percent.
email.body3:
Blair, last bit of proof for Sirona.

Memgraph had more in-market accounts than the team could touch and could not hire SDRs fast enough. They ran our AI SDR to $2.7M in pipeline, 600 replies, and 60 BANT-qualified deals in 90 days, same team, live in four weeks, every email auto-logged to their CRM.

I pulled a benchmark of how Sirona's reply rate likely compares to other Series-C health-tech startups. Want to hop on a quick call so I can walk you through it?
email.body4:

If tightening signal-to-meeting latency without adding headcount is not a priority this quarter, no problem at all. The post-raise stretch is its own kind of busy, and timing matters.

Before I close your file, worth 15 minutes to walk through a one-page playbook of three AI-SDR plays scoped to your RevOps motion? I will tailor it to Sirona either way.
